headline_marked: [[AI-generated Taipei GTA clone]] hits 1.2M concurrent players in 3 days, browser-based and free
headline: AI-generated Taipei GTA clone hits 1.2M concurrent players in 3 days, browser-based and free
summary: A free, browser-based game, Taipei GTA, created with $10,000 in AI tokens, has rapidly gained 1.2 million concurrent users, potentially drawing legal attention from Rockstar.
details: The browser-based game "Taipei GTA," developed by AICodeWith, has attracted 1.2 million concurrent users within just three days of its release. This free-to-play title, which cost an estimated $10,000 in AI coding tokens to create, is accessible directly via a web browser.

Despite its name potentially leading to legal challenges from Rockstar, the game remains online and fully playable. It appears to function as a showcase or demo for the AICodeWith platform, which offers access to over 30 AI models including DeepSeek, Qwen, and Kimi.

Hosted on the Vercel cloud platform, Taipei GTA features detailed zones based on real-world Taipei locations like Ximending and Chiang Kai-Shek Memorial Hall. The game captures the essence of the city with neon signage, motor scooters, convenience stores, and night markets.

Similar to the Grand Theft Auto series that inspired it, the game offers a free-roaming experience with criminal elements. Players begin on foot with minimal currency and can choose to explore the city or tackle 93 available missions.

Taipei GTA is currently under active development and expansion, with developers reportedly soliciting community feedback for future updates. Its low-poly models and simple lighting give it an early-2000s retrogaming aesthetic.

Performance is notably swift and responsive, even on integrated graphics, with reports of 100+ FPS on a Radeon 890M. This ensures a smooth experience for a wide range of users, despite the game's detailed urban environment.

headline_marked: [[Google launches Guided Vision]] for blind users, turning phones into conversational eyes
headline: Google launches Guided Vision for blind users, turning phones into conversational eyes
summary: Google's new Guided Vision feature for Gemini Live helps blind and low-vision users navigate physical tasks by turning their phone into a conversational set of eyes. It coaches users through framing and identifying objects.
details: Google is rolling out Guided Vision to Gemini Live as part of the September 2026 Android Drop. This new accessibility tool was built with and for blind and low-vision communities, transforming a smartphone into a conversational set of eyes.

The feature allows users to share their phone's live camera feed with Gemini Live and ask for assistance with physical tasks, such as locating a specific item on a shelf. Gemini processes the video feed and provides spoken directions.

Crucially, Guided Vision coaches users into a better shot if the camera isn't aimed correctly, prompting them to pan or adjust. It's integrated into Android, accessible via the TalkBack menu or accessibility shortcuts, and works on any phone running the Gemini app (Android 9+ with 2GB RAM), ensuring broad reach.

Unlike older visual assistance apps that require mode selection or process one image at a time, Guided Vision offers a continuous, back-and-forth dialogue. This conversational approach allows for follow-up questions and dynamic interaction with surroundings, bridging the gap between static software and live human assistance.

Google emphasizes that Guided Vision is not a medical device or mobility aid and does not replace safe-travel guides. The company warns that the AI can make mistakes and is not intended for navigation or real-time obstacle detection, drawing a clear line between identifying objects and ensuring safety in complex environments.
